flows.label: Tab
flows.description: Demo Playground, directory focused in normal mode, default demo rows, no modal, suggestions, macro recording or pending sequence: Tab runs input.next and focuses notes. Setup is shown first; subsequent steps follow the key and rendering. A source snapshot, not a recorded run.

steps.title: Setup binds Tab on the playground noun
steps.detail: The demo creates directory, notes and paths under agent, itself under playground (lines 61–85), and registers playground with directory as its initial focus (lines 88–105). bind stores rows on a noun, or on an input instance when the id names one. Tab and Shift-Tab are mode-less playground rows calling input.next; no key switch is involved.
steps.edge: After setup and opening Playground, a Tab key enters Update

steps.title: Update receives Tab
steps.detail: Bubble Tea v2 delivers tea.KeyPressMsg. Model.Update converts its String() to a MacroKey and calls handleKey. This is the same entry used for other live keys; paste has its own message case.
steps.edge: handleKey sends the MacroKey to the shared runtime dispatcher

steps.title: handleKey dispatches through the runtime
steps.detail: handleKey clears both status tones and calls DispatchOutcome. The runtime expires any old prefix, takes the current focus and mode, and calls dispatchIn (resolve.go:199–209). Macro recording uses a shadow mode there; this example has none. Errors go through the UI sink, and palette state is synchronized afterward.
steps.edge: dispatchIn builds the walk for the focused instance

steps.title: Ancestry follows Instance.Parent
steps.detail: The focus is an instance id. Ancestry follows Parent links outward, yielding directory, agent, playground, app. The resolver uses this order; Context paths use its reverse and an InputID for an input. This is instance ownership, with no layer overlay or frame context to replace.
steps.edge: stack adds the nouns and shared editor fallback to this ancestry

steps.title: Instance ancestry determines the key stack
steps.detail: With directory focused and no modal, the bubbling stack is directory → agent → playground → app → ochazuke.editor. The editor noun is a shared table fallback for writable inputs. walk/walkOf (lines 54–84) prepends an outer-first capture pass unless the base mode is passthrough. Open suggestions could add an inner level; none are open here. A top modal cuts off the page ancestry.
steps.edge: No capture row claims this key; bubbling consults each level’s tables
expect: out = append(out, level{inst: inst, noun: noun})

steps.title: The available tab row wins
steps.detail: lookup reads instance rows, then noun tables for the current mode and its inherited tables, plus mode-less rows when nonexclusive. It tests operation availability and row guards; exact keys rank before patterns (lines 377–477). No capture row answers here. The bubbling scan keeps the innermost hit, but waits if a longer applicable sequence exists anywhere before a class hit stops the scan. Here tab has no longer sequence, so the playground row runs input.next.
steps.edge: run records the answering level and invokes runRow
expect: r.lookup(lv, base, exclusive, prefix, sequence, key, ev)

steps.title: runRow executes the binding request
steps.detail: runRow records the key as the action source, handles one-shot pending modes, chooses the request target and fills any arguments sourced from the key. A missing required argument may open an args form. These requests are complete, so execute sets rowRequest and calls Runtime.Execute at the current focus context, then ExecuteAt canonicalizes aliases and records the outcome.
steps.edge: ExecuteAt calls execute for shared validation and handler selection

steps.title: Shared execution reaches input.next
steps.detail: ExecuteAt canonicalizes the request and calls execute. Earlier in execute, the operation and arguments, target, context, availability, subjects and verb checks are resolved. After confirmation handling, ActionFor can supply the innermost noun override; there is none for input.next in this example, so the registered operation’s Run handles it.
steps.edge: The registered input.next handler runs

steps.title: The demo handler chooses notes
steps.detail: input.next is a demo operation. It requires Playground with no open modal, locates c.InputID in directory / notes / paths, advances by delta (default 1, wrapping), and calls SetFocus. Starting at directory therefore chooses notes.
steps.edge: SetFocus validates notes and moves the runtime’s focus

steps.title: SetFocus updates focus and applies the mode rule
steps.detail: SetFocus first validates that notes belongs to the current page and is inside the top modal if one exists. setFocus clamps the id, cancels any prefix, assigns Runtime.Focus and calls focusMoved. Moving from directory to the unpinned notes stop resets the base mode to normal (focusMoved, lines 97–113); the input follows that mode.
steps.edge: The handler and dispatcher return to Model.Update

steps.title: Update returns queued commands
steps.detail: Control returns to Update. It observes ticker state, settles placement notes and checks quit. For this non-quitting key it collects redraw, sequence-timeout, delivery/job and other scheduled commands, then returns tea.Batch. Rendering happens through Bubble Tea’s View phase; neither the handler nor SetFocus calls View.
steps.edge: Bubble Tea renders through Model.View and render

steps.title: View renders the current page around notes
steps.detail: Model.View calls render and returns a tea.View with its cursor (lines 947–956). render uses Runtime.Page, not a retained Frame, and calls pageContent to render the registered Playground page. The runtime now focuses notes. keepFocusShown may retarget an undrawn stop and redraw; notes is drawn here, so its focus is retained.

flows.label: Ctrl-N
flows.description: Demo Playground, directory focused in normal mode, default demo rows, no modal, suggestions, macro recording or pending sequence: Ctrl-N opens draft around the registered dialog input and keeps the page underneath. Setup is shown first. A source snapshot, not a recorded run.

steps.title: Setup binds Ctrl-N and registers the draft renderer
steps.detail: The playground noun binds ctrl+n only in normal mode, to modal.push with id=draft and input=dialog. dialog was registered under app (lines 62–85). ModalViews["draft"] is a demo renderer that draws InputBlock for Runtime.ModalFocus (lines 111–124). Neither the page noun nor the renderer creates a frame.
steps.edge: On Playground with directory focused in normal mode, Ctrl-N enters Update

steps.title: Update receives Ctrl-N

expect: r.lookup(lv, base, exclusive, prefix, sequence, key, ev)

steps.title: runRow executes the binding request
steps.detail: runRow records the key as the action source, handles one-shot pending modes, chooses the request target and fills any arguments sourced from the key. A missing required argument may open an args form. These requests are complete, so execute sets rowRequest and calls Runtime.Execute at the current focus context, then ExecuteAt canonicalizes aliases and records the outcome.
steps.edge: ExecuteAt calls execute for shared validation and handler selection

steps.title: Shared execution reaches ochazuke.modal.push
steps.detail: ExecuteAt canonicalizes the request and calls execute. Earlier in execute, the operation and arguments, target, context, availability, subjects and verb checks are resolved. After confirmation handling, ActionFor can supply the innermost noun override; there is none for ochazuke.modal.push in this example, so the registered operation’s Run handles it.
steps.edge: The registered ochazuke.modal.push handler runs

steps.title: modal.push passes a registered input to Push
steps.detail: The framework operation’s canonical noun is ochazuke.modal (modal is its short alias). It checks that dialog is a registered input and calls Push("draft", "dialog"), returning the resulting context. No InputPaths lookup or Frame construction remains.
steps.edge: Push creates a modal instance and remembers where it opened

steps.title: Push saves the return place and adopts dialog
steps.detail: Push rejects an empty or already-open id and an opener beneath another modal. draft does not exist, so it registers an ochazuke.modal instance under app. It cancels pending keys, stores the old focus in Payload.Return and the old base mode in returnMode, then appends draft to the modal stack. Because dialog was outside its subtree, Push saves dialog’s parent and temporarily parents it under draft. setFocus("dialog") applies the normal focus/mode rule and emits the surface-open event. The page remains registered underneath; Pop will restore the borrowed parent and return place.
steps.edge: The modal operation, runtime dispatcher and handleKey return to Update

steps.title: Update returns queued commands
steps.detail: Control returns to Update. It observes ticker state, settles placement notes and checks quit. For this non-quitting key it collects redraw, sequence-timeout, delivery/job and other scheduled commands, then returns tea.Batch. Rendering happens through Bubble Tea’s View phase; neither the handler nor SetFocus calls View.
steps.edge: Bubble Tea renders through Model.View and render

steps.title: Rendering asks the draft’s ModalView for its body
steps.detail: After Update, Model.View calls render. It renders the page with beneath’s saved focus/mode, restores the live modal focus, and walks Runtime.modals. modalContent resolves ModalFocus and dispatches to the registered ModalViews renderer, here the demo’s draft InputBlock. A self-drawing component or plain input is a fallback when no explicit renderer exists.
steps.edge: The rendered body is composed over the page shell

steps.title: render composes each modal over the page
steps.detail: render iterates the modal ids in stack order, obtains each body, applies its viewport and builds hints from the modal focus’s binding rows. modalBlock composes draft above the page surface, hiding the cursor beneath it. Subsequent keys resolve within dialog → draft → modal noun → app → editor; the covered playground ancestry is excluded by stack’s modal boundary.
expect: surface = m.modalBlock(id, layout, surface.Text, title, body

flows.label: g g
flows.description: Sandbox with g g=go-top, normal mode, no competing g binding or longer sequence: press g twice before its configured deadline (CLI default 400 ms). The first key enters a pending prefix mode; the second runs the dummy action. Setup is shown first. A source snapshot, not a live key log.

steps.title: The sandbox installs a declarative g g row
steps.detail: Setup installs g g=go-top as an app noun row in mode "" and registers sandbox.go-top, whose handler writes the latest history result. Assume no competing g row or longer g g sequence, normal mode, and sandbox started. runKeybinding defaults --timeout to 400 ms and assigns Runtime.BindingTimeout (lines 185–207); this host override differs from the framework’s default sequence-timeout of 0 (wait indefinitely).
steps.edge: The first g arrives as a Tea key press

steps.title: Sandbox Update receives the first g
steps.detail: Once sandbox mode is active, Update forwards each tea.KeyPressMsg to handleKey(msg.String(), false). Paste is logged separately and is not dispatched. Timeout messages go to handleTimeout. This trace follows two g presses before the 400 ms deadline, not a timeout.
steps.edge: handleKey logs g and invokes the same runtime used by Model

steps.title: handleKey records g and calls HandleBinding
steps.detail: The sandbox adds g to its bounded history and initializes its result to unmatched. HandleBinding is a named-key adapter to Dispatch(MacroKey{Key: key}); Dispatch uses DispatchOutcome. On return, a nonempty Runtime.Pending displays pending: g, and the host returns BindingTimeoutCommand to Bubble Tea.
steps.edge: HandleBinding delegates to DispatchOutcome and dispatchIn

steps.title: DispatchOutcome resolves the current mode and focus
steps.detail: DispatchOutcome expires a deadline that already passed, captures Runtime.Focus and Runtime.Mode, and enters dispatchIn. On the first g no prefix is held, so sequence is g. On the second g, baseAndPrefix splits the pending normal g mode and joins its held g with the new key to form g g. No macro is recording.
steps.edge: lookup examines the app noun’s mode-less g g row

steps.title: lookup finds a longer available sequence
steps.detail: The instance and noun tables include mode-less rows when nonexclusive. lookup ignores unbound rows, rows from the wrong capture pass, unavailable requests and false guards. g is a strict prefix of the sandbox’s g g row, so look.longer becomes true. A generated prefix-cancel row alone never causes a wait. There is no completed g match in this setup.
steps.edge: The bubbling scan sees look.longer and waits

steps.title: The whole-stack scan chooses to wait
steps.detail: The capture pass has no hit. The bubbling pass collects look results across the stack, retaining an innermost completed match if one exists. A longer applicable sequence makes look.waits true and calls wait(exact), rather than immediately running a shorter hit. Here exact is nil; wait calls enterPrefix("normal", "g", nil).
steps.edge: enterPrefix represents the sequence as a pending mode

steps.title: The prefix mode holds g and arms its deadline
steps.detail: enterPrefix calls enterMode with name normal g and Payload.Prefix=g; the saved Request is nil. enterMode (lines 654–662) saves the base mode in Payload.Return and calls armPrefix. armPrefix publishes Runtime.Pending=g, increments the timer generation and records the focus/mode. In this sandbox the positive BindingTimeout override supplies a 400 ms deadline.
steps.edge: handleKey sees Pending=g and returns the timer command

steps.title: The custom Tea host schedules the timeout once
steps.detail: BindingTimeoutCommand returns a command for a pending, still-current prefix with a finite deadline. It marks it scheduled and captures the current generation. If the second g completes the sequence first, leaving the prefix invalidates this timer; HandleBindingTimeout ignores the stale generation. With the framework’s default infinite wait this method schedules nothing.
steps.edge: Before the deadline, the second g repeats Update → handleKey → DispatchOutcome

steps.title: The second g completes g g and leaves the prefix
steps.detail: The same dispatchIn entry joins the held prefix and new key into g g (lines 218–222). lookup now finds the exact sandbox row, with no longer sequence. The scan calls run(hitLv, hit) (lines 301–307). run leaves the prefix before executing the row, restores the base mode and invalidates the first g’s timer. It then calls runRow with the answering app level.
steps.edge: runRow executes sandbox.go-top through the shared operation path

steps.title: runRow executes the binding request
steps.detail: runRow records the key as the action source, handles one-shot pending modes, chooses the request target and fills any arguments sourced from the key. A missing required argument may open an args form. These requests are complete, so execute sets rowRequest and calls Runtime.Execute at the current focus context, then ExecuteAt canonicalizes aliases and records the outcome.
steps.edge: ExecuteAt calls execute for shared validation and handler selection

steps.title: sandbox.go-top records ACTION: go-top
steps.detail: Execute → ExecuteAt → execute validate the request and call the registered operation’s Run (runtime.go:857–1020). This sandbox handler changes no editor cursor: go-top is a user-selected label for a dummy action. It writes ACTION: go-top to the second g’s history slot and returns the action name. handleKey keeps this result because Pending is now empty and the slot is no longer unmatched.
steps.edge: Update returns; Bubble Tea renders the sandbox result

steps.title: The sandbox renders its latest key and history
steps.detail: The sandbox’s own View creates a tea.View from render (lines 125–128). render shows the latest quoted key and its ACTION result, the configured runtime timeout, effective sandbox bindings, and the history newest first. The first g remains pending: g in history; the second g shows ACTION: go-top. This is a source-backed example, not a recorded key log.
